evidence: The PR changed Dolt created_at/updated_at ordering from varchar text to time.Time with no test pinning it. The reviewer's conformance case couldn't be built because CreateIssueInput carries no timestamps and there is no clock seam. The agent added an engine-local test that sets created_at directly, confirmed by mutation that it fails, and filed the suite gap as utz7.
guidance_note: When a refactor changes the comparison semantics of a key as a side effect, add the test that pins the new semantics in the same PR, using the cheapest layer that can construct the colliding input.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. e6a14f4 only added list_time_order_test.go and a CHANGELOG sentence. The duplicated issueOrdering fold came from the original round-0 commit, and the agent says so: it had already filed the duplication as links-store-seam-firh before review and deferred it. The extraction to storage.IssueOrdering in 00daf33 was a net -12 lines, and its mutation table was reported, including a coverage gap on Dolt.
guidance_note: When a change makes two engines' mechanisms identical, extract the shared composition in the same PR instead of filing a ticket to defer duplication you just created.

narrative: Status sort was moved past hydration in both engines. Round 0 asked for a test of the timestamp-ordering change that came along with it, and the agent put the test in the engine suite because the conformance suite had no clock seam. Round 1 flagged duplication that the original commit introduced and the agent had knowingly deferred, plus an out-of-diff stale godoc on ListIssues. Neither round-1 issue came from the round-0 fix.
guidance_observations: The agent had already spotted the round-1 duplication before review and deferred it to a ticket; acting on it before opening the PR would have saved the round.
The ListIssues godoc that went stale was a fourth doc site the ticket's 'three sites move together' list missed; grepping for the old behavior's wording before the first push would have caught it.

evidence: The NewEngine type became func(t, clock), and the package doc example still showed func(t *testing.T) storage.Store. Code copied from that example would not compile. Fixed in 032f65d.
guidance_note: When changing an exported function type's signature, grep the package doc and examples for the old shape before pushing.

evidence: The hand-copied comparator was real duplication. But the proposed slices.IsSortedFunc(events, storage.EventOrdering) would make the production function the oracle of the test that exists to pin it, and the agent showed by mutation that reversing EventOrdering would then pass. The agent rewrote the case as two keyed assertions and moved the reviewer's fix to sameIssueInOrder, a third copy the reviewer had not flagged.
guidance_note: When extracting a rule into one function, sweep every spelled-out copy in the same change, and decide for each one whether it is a consumer (delegate to the function) or the rule's own test (keep an independent oracle).

evidence: memory.New gained a 'clock is required' refusal, and no test called it with a nil clock; newEngineWithWorkspace always passed SystemClock. A table row for the nil clock was added, and removing the refusal makes it fail.
guidance_note: Every new refusal added at a constructor gets a test row in the same commit, especially when an existing comment already claims plural refusals are covered.

evidence: The reviewer reported the same stale doc example as F1 a second time. The agent pointed out the duplicate, and the single fix in 032f65d closed both.
guidance_note: When changing an exported function type's signature, grep the package doc and examples for the old shape before pushing.

evidence: The Dolt engine had 17 call sites, and the memory engine's deleted now() wrapper was an 18th, but the CHANGELOG said 'seventeen ... across the two engines'. The agent also found the same wrong count in clock.go's godoc and fixed both places in 98aebd3.
guidance_note: Before writing a count into a changelog or godoc, derive it with a grep over the removed lines in both packages rather than one.

narrative: This PR added a clock seam to the storage contract. Round 0 raised five findings, all about the original diff: a stale doc example reported twice, a duplicated comparator, a missing nil-clock test, and a wrong count. The agent pushed back with evidence on the reviewer's tautological-oracle fix, applied that fix where it belonged, and swept a second home of the wrong count. Round 1 was clean.
guidance_observations: Three of the five findings were the original diff's own residue: an example, a count, and a comparator copy. A grep for the old signature and the extracted rule before the first push would have closed them.

evidence: PR #488 deleted internal/store/list_time_order_test.go, but the q35v.6 Fixed bullet in the same Unreleased section still named that file and called utz7 open. The agent checked that the file was absent and appended one sentence before promotion froze the entry. This drift crossed PRs and has no earlier finding inside this PR.
guidance_note: When a PR deletes a file or closes a ticket, grep the Unreleased CHANGELOG for that path and ticket id and amend the earlier entries in the same PR.

narrative: A one-line release promotion. The reviewer caught a contradiction inside the changelog left behind by PR #488, which deleted a test file that an earlier Unreleased bullet still cited. The agent fixed it with one appended sentence, and round 1 approved.
guidance_observations: The defect came from #488's PR, which removed the file without sweeping the CHANGELOG entries that referenced it; promotion was the last chance to fix it before the entry froze.

evidence: The agent confirmed that inlineSyncFailure switched only on ProsePending and Unrelated, and that settledCleanly rejected IDCollision, so the inline receive was silent. 376e9ed added the case and threaded collisions through reconcileOutcome. The plan also promised a traceStatus change that the fix then deliberately did not make, which F12 later picked up.
guidance_note: When adding a value to an enum-like state type, grep every switch over that type and wire each one before the first push, instead of only the surface you were working on.

evidence: Both exports come from the same Store, so Export stamps s.workspaceID on both sides. The agent checked the reviewer's option (a), found that the workspace_id meta row is rewritten with the local id on every schema reconcile, rejected (a) on that evidence, and took option (b): drop the fields and label the sides local/remote.
guidance_note: Before reporting a provenance field to an operator, trace where both sides' values come from and check in an end-to-end test that they can differ.

evidence: mergeAndReplay is also reached from SyncReconcileCombine with an empty base, which is the Classify CreatedAt fallback, and no end-to-end test covered it. TestSyncReconcileCombineRefusesIDCollision was added.
guidance_note: When a new check sits in a function with several callers, write an end-to-end test per caller, and put the base-less fallback path first.

evidence: The SyncPull switch at store/sync.go:269-311 fell to 'unhandled reconcile state', even though a comment in the PR claimed all three surfaces behave the same. SyncPullIDCollision and Collisions were added and wired through syncFailureFromPull, with tests.
guidance_note: When adding a value to an enum-like state type, grep every switch over that type and wire each one before the first push, instead of only the surface you were working on.

evidence: This finding has the same root as F1 and F4: two switches over SyncReconcileState missed the new value. Both were fixed in 376e9ed, and the 'surface identically' comment became true instead of being softened.
guidance_note: When adding a value to an enum-like state type, grep every switch over that type and wire each one before the first push, instead of only the surface you were working on.

evidence: The ownerNotifyKind doc still said 'three divergence kinds' after a fourth was added. The count was dropped, along with a sibling comment in the same file. The same stale 'three' in owner_notify_test.go was missed, and it came back as F20.
guidance_note: When dropping a stale count from a comment, grep the package's tests and docs for the same count and phrase as well as the file you are in.

evidence: The agent found harm beyond the reviewer's type argument: child-table merges unioned both tickets' comments, relations and events onto the colliding id. It replaced issueSet with a per-side issueScope and moved the gate onto Provisional() returning (Export, bool), which is broader than the reviewer's ApplyProseResolutions-only check. This fix later produced F9, F10 and F17.
guidance_note: When moving a gate onto an accessor, list every caller of that accessor, decide what each caller does with ok=false, and test each one in the same commit.

evidence: The SyncReconcile, SyncReconcileCombine and mergeAndReplay docs still described two outcomes after the collision refusal made three. Each doc gained one clause.
guidance_note: When adding an outcome to a function, update the doc comment of every function that lists that function's outcomes before pushing.

evidence: The `if !ok { return model.Export{}, false }` gate in ApplyProseResolutions was added by F7's fix in 376e9ed, and no test exercised it. 6d8ca59 added a test with an exact bijection where only the gate can refuse, and the agent checked by mutation that the test fails without the gate.
guidance_note: A safety-net gate added to answer a finding ships with a test that reaches only that gate, in the same commit.

evidence: F7's fix made Provisional() return ok=false. foldStepper.step began checking it, but on ok=false it returned a bare fmt.Errorf, so the collision reached every surface as an opaque error. The agent conceded: 'the previous round fixed the fusion here and left the reporting behind.' The cause was the same class of gap as F1/F4/F5: a new failure path not wired to the reported state.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new detection point for an existing failure state, route it through the same state conversion as the original detection before pushing, instead of returning a raw error.

evidence: The two added lines at sync_reconcile_cmd.go:340 also offset round 0's F5 hunk (@@ -452 +454), so this dead case came from the original PR and not from a fix. The agent checked that neither call site is reached from the IDCollision branch and deleted the case.
guidance_note: Before adding an arm to a mapping function, check that a call site actually passes the new value; if none does, the arm is a second copy waiting to drift.

evidence: The reviewer was right that the F1 plan promised a traceStatus change that never landed. But 'ok' is consistent with ProsePending and Unrelated, and Decision=id_collision is already the precise scan key, so the substantive change would have been a collision-only inconsistency. The finding exists only because the F1 plan reply overpromised, and the reviewer itself offered 'drop the claim if ok is intentional'.
guidance_note: Keep fix-plan replies to the finding's scope; an extra fix promised in a plan and then not made becomes its own review finding.

evidence: The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply opens 'Plan: valid' and the parenthetical was updated in 6d8ca59. The table row and the stale paragraph were both in the original docs change, not in a fix.
guidance_note: When adding a value to an enumerated table in docs, update every prose list of the same set on that page.

evidence: The original PR made combine refuse the whole operation on a collision, but the combine bullet still said 'every issue kept'. The bullet now states the exception and cross-references the new section.
guidance_note: When a change narrows a command's guarantee, grep the docs for each place that states the old guarantee about that command.

evidence: The reportReconcileResult IDCollision branch came from the original PR, and unlike its Unrelated sibling it had no direct test. b7fce33 added two tests mirroring TestReportReconcileResultUnrelated*; they appear in the 78555a4 diff.
guidance_note: When a new branch says it mirrors a sibling, copy the sibling's tests along with its code.

evidence: The original describeCollisionSide put remote issue.Title and Description verbatim inside the <agent-instructions> envelope. The F2 fix only changed the side labels, so this was pre-existing. The agent reproduced the injection by reverting, built the quoteRemote choke point with defuse and fence, and filed the same exposure in prose_pending.go as links-sync-87j7.
guidance_note: Before embedding any field from another machine into an agent-instruction envelope, route it through a quoting type, decided when the renderer is written.

evidence: The flagged commit 78555a4 only touches cli files, so the flag is positional. The real source is fold-level collision detection, added by the F7 and F10 fixes, which runs only after settle; a fold-only collision therefore waits behind prose pending on another id. The reviewer itself framed this as a possible accepted trade-off, and the agent documented the trade-off in a comment and rejected the eager full-chain export.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a detection point late in a pipeline, write down in the same commit which earlier exits can mask it.

evidence: 78555a4, the F16 fix, added the comment 'they reach the envelope only through quoteRemoteText', but the function is named quoteRemote. The flag on e6a3e80 is positional: that commit only changed a sync_reconcile.go comment. The rename landed in a follow-up PR because of the round cap, so this PR merged with the wrong name.
guidance_note: After naming a new function in a comment, grep the comment's identifier against the tree before committing.

evidence: quoteRemote, added in 78555a4, split only on \n after normalizing \r\n and \r, so U+2028 kept an unmarked logical line, and ESC/ANSI codes passed through to a terminal. The follow-up widened the normalizer and replaced control characters with U+FFFD instead of dropping them, and the agent noted that dropping them could splice a live delimiter back together. The fix shipped in a follow-up PR, not this one.
guidance_note: When writing a sanitizer for untrusted text, list the full set of line-break and control code points a downstream reader may honor before choosing what to normalize, instead of only \n and \r.

evidence: F6's fix dropped 'three' from two owner_notify.go comments but did not sweep owner_notify_test.go, whose loop and comment still listed three classes. The flag on e6a3e80 is positional. Rounds 2 and 3 had already raised this as out-of-diff summary findings and it went unaddressed until it came back inline. The fix landed in a follow-up PR.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale enumeration, grep the package's tests for the same enumerated set as well as the comment that was flagged.

evidence: The flag is positional. e6a3e80 was comment-only, and the Classify ancestry short-circuit dates from the original PR. The agent checked the reachable hard-delete path through replaceFromExport/deleteIssueTx and that new child ids are max+1 over live rows. It implemented the reviewer's own suggestion, a base CreatedAt match, and noted that TestClassifyAncestryOutranksBirthCertificate had been pinning the defect. The fix shipped in a follow-up PR.
guidance_note: When an invariant is called 'proof', write the test that tries to break it, here by deleting the id and re-minting it on both sides, before trusting a fixture that happens to fit the defect.

evidence: The F16 fix's own rationale said that defusing tags alone leaves an imperative intact, yet its inline() method for remote ids applied no fence or boundary. The agent bounded inline() values with «» and labeled the inventory heading as data, instead of fencing each id. It kept the inventory readable and offered to escalate to full fencing. The fix landed in a follow-up PR.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces two rendering modes for the same untrusted input, apply the fix's own threat argument to each mode before pushing.

narrative: This PR added id-collision refusal to reconcile. Round 0 found the new state wired into only one of three surfaces, plus doc and test gaps. The broader F7 gate on Provisional() produced an untested gate (F9) and a fold path that raised a raw error (F10), and F10's fold detection then left a deferral gap behind prose pending (F17). The F16 security fix introduced quoteRemote, and round 4 found three gaps in it: a wrong name in a comment, missing Unicode/control handling, and unbounded ids rendered inline. The reviewer then hit its five-round cap, so the agent split the round-4 fixes into a follow-up PR and merged at e6a3e80 with those defects still open.
guidance_observations: Adding a state value without first listing every switch over its type cost three round-0 findings (F1, F4, F5) with one root cause.
Out-of-diff summary findings in rounds 2 and 3 about owner_notify_test.go went unaddressed until they came back inline in round 4; summary-only findings need the same triage as inline threads.

Fixes that introduced new mechanisms (the Provisional gate, quoteRemote) each produced the next round's findings; applying the fix's own argument to every caller and mode before pushing would have collapsed rounds.
Hitting the round cap forced a merge with acknowledged open security gaps; the agent's correction comments say so explicitly.
